findings.issue_text: [BUG] `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` is not a valid Java call — `picocli` is a package name (only `import picocli.CommandLine;` is present), so this is a compile error; there is no static `exit` accessor reachable via a bare package identifier, and picocli exposes no such member on `CommandLine` anyway. The quarkus runtime module fails to compile, breaking the whole build; the feature-disabled guard never ships and the documented exit-code-4 behavior cannot exist.

[BUG] Same fabricated `picocli.exit(...)` reference as UpdateCompatibilityCheck — package name used as an invocable object with no `picocli` field or static import in scope. Compile error in the quarkus runtime module; the guard and FEATURE_DISABLED exit code are unbuildable.

[BUG] The test now calls `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec()` / `setFeatureSpec(new FeatureSpec())` / `getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(...)`, but no CRD class change appears in this diff — the v2alpha1 `KeycloakDeploymentSpec` API the test previously used (`getUnsupported()`/`UnsupportedSpec`) is replaced with a `FeatureSpec` API that the diff does not introduce, so these methods do not exist on the current CRD model. The operator integration test module fails to compile; the rolling-updates upgrade test cannot run, hiding the very behavior this PR is meant to validate.

[BUG] The documented example sets `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` on the Keycloak CR, but the v2alpha1 Keycloak CRD used by the operator has no `spec.features` field (feature toggles live under the unsupported-spec mechanism), and this diff adds no CRD field or operator code that reads `spec.features`. Operators who copy the documented CR get a rejected/dropped field and the rolling-updates feature is never enabled, hitting the very Operator failure the new CAUTION block warns about.

[ADVISORY] `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` silently changes from 4 to 3 and 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, with no change to any consumer that parsed exit code 4 as 'recreate required'. Any external automation or the operator parsing the documented exit code 4 (previously recreate) now interprets the new 'recreate' value 3 as an error and treats 'feature disabled' (4) as the recreate case during rolling upgrades; who gets bitten: script-based rolling-upgrade orchestrators between versions.

[ADVISORY] The template hard-appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every rendered `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility ${parameters}` snippet for all environments, including the metadata-save example, making the docs assume the feature is always enabled rather than documenting the prerequisite. Users on non-preview or custom builds get 'Unable to use this command' errors from copy-pasted commands whenever the flag is stripped by their wrapper scripts; also the upgrade-check example in the guide now enables the feature on the new server while the old server's saved metadata was produced without it, so the check compares across differing feature sets.

[BUG] The docs promise 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when rolling-updates is disabled, but this diff contains zero operator-side enforcement code — no check of Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ROLLING_UPDATES) or equivalent in any operator source file — so the documented failure behavior is not implemented by the changes shown. An operator user who sets spec.update.strategy without enabling the feature gets whatever the operator's default/ungated behavior is (likely a silent successful reconcile or an unrelated error), not the documented hard failure; the acceptance criterion stated in the shipped documentation cannot be met by the code in this PR.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), and no test anywhere in the diff asserts the new RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE value (3) after the change from 4 to 3. A regression in either exit code (e.g., CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED accidentally reusing an existing code, or the recreate check returning the old 4) passes CI; downstream automation and the operator, which branch on these exit codes, silently take the wrong upgrade path.

[ADVISORY] The operator integration tests are only updated to enable the feature in the happy-path deployment (setFeatureSpec + setEnabledFeatures) with no negative test covering a Keycloak CR with spec.update set but rolling-updates disabled — the exact scenario the new documentation CAUTION describes. The operator test suite never exercises the documented failure mode, so the CLI-facing gating (docs table row 4, 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature rolling-updates is disabled.') has no operator-side verification; an operator user bitten by the disabled-feature path has no test evidence that the operator reports it as compatibility result 4 rather than crashing or reconciling incorrectly.

[ADVISORY] The docs exit-code table adds row 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED but contains no row or note documenting that the recreate-upgrade exit code moved from 4 to 3 (CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE change), a silent breaking change to a public CLI contract with no migration note. Existing automation (upgrade pipelines, scripts, and any tooling that wraps `kc.sh update-compatibility check`) written against the old exit code 4 now either misclassifies 'recreate required' as 'feature disabled' or treats it as an unknown/software error; operators get bitten on the first upgraded deployment.

[BUG] The PR silently renumbers the existing public exit code RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 to make room for FEATURE_DISABLED=4, a breaking change to the documented CLI contract that is not traceable to the stated intent (adding a feature flag). Any operator script, CI pipeline, or wrapper that already branches on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate upgrade required' now receives 3 for that case and 4 for a completely different condition (feature disabled), so automation silently takes the wrong branch after upgrade.

[ADVISORY] The new CAUTION claims the Operator will fail when rolling-updates is not enabled, but this diff contains no operator-side gating code — only a Feature enum entry, a test, and a Dockerfile change — so the documented enforcement is not implemented anywhere in the reviewed changes. Operators following the doc will rely on a failure mode that the shipped operator code in this PR does not produce (or produces in a separate unreviewed commit), leaving the doc claiming behavior with no traceable implementation.

[ADVISORY] The test refactor swaps the deprecated UnsupportedSpec wiring for the new FeatureSpec API and reorders setUpdateSpec, an unrelated spec-migration bundled into a feature-flag PR. Future maintainers bisecting operator CRD-spec behavior changes must untangle this migration from the rolling-updates flag work; if FeatureSpec backport availability differs from UnsupportedSpec, the test's environment assumptions drift silently.

[ADVISORY] Baking --features=rolling-updates into the shared custom test image permanently enables a preview feature for every consumer of that image, not just the rolling-update tests this PR is about. Any other operator integration test using the custom image now runs with an unrequested preview feature enabled, masking feature-off code paths and coupling unrelated test results to this PR's flag.

[ADVISORY] The new testFeatureNotEnabled test asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4) that the new command path returns, leaving the one new behavior-bearing branch (early return with picocli.exit) without contract coverage. A regression that returns exit code 0 (success) while printing the error text would pass the test and silently report success to the automation the exit-code contract exists for.

[BUG] The diff silently changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and repurposes exit code 4 as FEATURE_DISABLED, so the meaning of exit code 4 changes from 'recreate upgrade required' to 'rolling-updates feature disabled'. Any existing automation/script (CI pipelines, operator upgrade logic, admin tooling) that branches on exit code 4 == 'recreate upgrade required' now misclassifies: recreate-required cases return 3 (which such scripts treat as an unknown/software error) and feature-disabled cases return 4 and are misinterpreted as recreate-required, triggering a full shutdown that was never needed. This is an unversioned breaking change to a documented CLI contract (the update-compatibility exit-code table) with no versioning or compatibility note for the old mapping.

[ADVISORY] The rolling-updates feature must be baked into the server image at build time (--features=rolling-updates on kc.sh build) for the update-compatibility commands to work, coupling the operator's upgrade path to a custom image build step rather than runtime configuration. Operators running the stock keycloak image (or any image built without the flag) get a hard failure of the update-compatibility tooling and, per the new CAUTION in advanced-configuration.adoc, the Operator itself; the failure surfaces only at upgrade time, not at deployment time, so an operator who enables spec.update.strategy=Recreate without rebuilding their image discovers the breakage during an actual upgrade attempt. The diff contains no runtime feature-flag path (env var / start argument) for the operator's own invocation of these commands, making the Dockerfile the only integration point.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled path calls picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) and returns, but the exit code 4 is not in picocli.CommandLine.ExitCode's standard set and is undocumented as an error path distinct from the tool's compatibility verdicts, mixing 'configuration error' semantics into the same exit-code channel the tool uses for its documented result table. The update-compatibility guide's table now conflates compatibility outcomes (0-3) with a configuration prerequisite failure (4); consumers parsing the table cannot tell from the docs whether 4 is a verdict or an invocation error, and the ordering means a misconfigured invocation (feature off) is indistinguishable in kind from a compatibility finding, inviting scripts to treat FEATURE_DISABLED as a recreate verdict (the pre-existing meaning of 4).

[ADVISORY] The docs template unconditionally appends --features=rolling-updates to every update-compatibility example, which becomes wrong the moment the feature is promoted to default/GA, and the template has no mechanism to reflect that state change. Doc readers copy the flag verbatim; once the feature graduates (or in an environment where the flag is already set via env/KC_FEATURES), the flag is redundant, and at GA removal of the preview feature the documented command fails with an unrecognized-feature error. The doc and the feature lifecycle are now manually coupled with no single source of truth for whether the flag is required.

[BUG] The diff silently renumbers RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 to make room for FEATURE_DISABLED=4, changing the tool's documented exit-code contract without any human sign-off note in the change. Any operator, CI job, or customer automation written against the previously documented exit code 4 = 'recreate upgrade required' now interprets that case as exit code 3, and a run returning 4 is read as 'feature disabled' — existing deployments' automation takes the wrong branch on the first upgraded binary, e.g. proceeding with a rolling upgrade plan when a recreate is actually required.

[ADVISORY] Both update-compatibility subcommands now hard-fail when the rolling-updates feature is disabled, converting a previously working (preview) CLI into a no-op gated on a flag unrelated to the command's original intent of checking compatibility. Existing users of `kc.sh update-compatibility` who upgrade the server without passing --features=rolling-updates get 'Unable to use this command' instead of the compatibility assessment they relied on; there is no deprecation period or escape hatch other than enabling a preview feature.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 and 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, so pre-existing operator/CI automation that branches on exit code 4 == 'recreate upgrade required' will now misclassify a disabled-feature failure. Operators who scripted `kc.sh update-compatibility` against the previously documented exit code 4 will see a disabled-feature condition exit as 3 (or treat 4 differently), misclassifying upgrade-safety verdicts during upgrade automation; the docs in this same diff redefine the table but out-of-tree consumers get no migration signal.

[ADVISORY] The upgrade-safety verification tool is hard-gated behind a preview feature flag, so on a default deployment the only pre-upgrade compatibility check is unavailable (exit 4) rather than degraded-but-usable. An operator upgrading a stock (non-preview) Keycloak deployment runs `update-compatibility check` as the pre-flight safety check, gets a feature-disabled error instead of the compatibility verdict, and must enable a preview feature just to verify upgrade safety — reducing the availability of a safety control at exactly the moment it matters.

[BUG] testWrongVersions asserts only the error message and never the exit code, so the behavioral change of RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 in this diff (CompatibilityResult.java:34) is completely unverified. The exit-code contract is consumed by the Keycloak Operator's update logic; if the recreate-incompatible path regressed to exit code 4 (now FEATURE_DISABLED), every existing test in this file still passes and the operator misclassifies recreate-required deployments as feature-disabled failures. The only exit-code assertion in the entire diff is assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()) in testCompatible, which covers a code path whose value did not change.

[BUG] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error string and never asserts that the process exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), the new exit-code value this diff introduces. The new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code — documented as outcome '4' in update-compatibility.adoc and relied on by operators/scripts parsing CLI output — is never verified anywhere; a regression returning the wrong code (e.g. picocli's generic SOFTWARE exit code 1) passes the test because assertError only matches a substring of stderr.

[ADVISORY] The diff modifies UpgradeTest to unconditionally enable the rolling-updates feature in every parameterized deployment, and no test anywhere in the diff exercises the documented failure mode where the feature is disabled. The diff's own documentation (advanced-configuration.adoc) states 'the Operator will fail' when the feature is disabled while an update strategy is set — that operator-side guard behavior, a new branch, is never triggered by any test; the next contributor changing that guard (or breaking it) ships with a green operator suite. Checked operator/src/test/** changes in this diff: only UpgradeTest.java was touched, and only to add the feature to the spec, never to verify its absence.

[ADVISORY] testMissingOptionOnSave's sole assertion is assertNoMessage("Missing required argument") — a negative assertion that passes regardless of whether the command behaves correctly, including when it fails for the wrong reason. The metadata subcommand run with the feature enabled but a missing required option has its actual failure mode (exit code, error text, whether validateConfig runs before or after the feature gate) unverified; a change making this command crash with an unhandled exception instead of a usage error still passes this test, since an unhandled exception also produces no 'Missing required argument' line.

[ADVISORY] The `update-compatibility check` exit code contract is silently renumbered in this diff: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3, and 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, with no compat shim or version gate for existing consumers. Any existing automation (operator upgrade logic or operator/user scripts already shipped against the prior release) that branches on exit code 4 == 'recreate upgrade required' now interprets a recreate-required result as 'feature disabled' and a feature-disabled result as 'recreate required', producing the wrong remediation path during an upgrade-window decision; this is exactly the expand/contract violation of changing a cross-process contract in one step.

[BUG] FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 silently collides with the previously documented RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4, and the recreate exit code is changed from 4 to 3 in the same diff, so any existing consumer of the documented CLI contract misclassifies results. Automation written against the previously documented exit code 4 ('Rolling Upgrade is not possible, recreate required') now receives 4 for a completely different condition — the feature being disabled — and scripts checking `exit == 4` will conclude a recreate upgrade is needed when the command actually never ran the compatibility check, silently skipping the compatibility verification the tool exists to provide. Conversely, scripts expecting 4 for recreate now get 3 and fall into their generic-error/default path. No versioned or documented migration of the exit-code contract is included other than a table row, so pre-existing consumers break silently.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled check calls picocli.exit(4) and returns before printPreviewWarning() and validateConfig() run, so a user invoking the command with both the feature disabled AND an invalid config gets only the feature message, masking the config error. Operators debugging why a compatibility check fails see only the 'rolling-updates is not enabled' error even when their configuration is also broken; after enabling the feature they hit the config error in a second, separate failure round-trip. This is minor but the ordering makes the first error report incomplete about the full set of problems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff silently changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and repurposes exit code 4 as FEATURE_DISABLED, so the meaning of exit code 4 changes from 'recreate upgrade required' to 'rolling-updates feature disabled'. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rolling-updates feature must be baked into the server image at build time (--features=rolling-updates on kc.sh build) for the update-compatibility commands to work, coupling the operator's upgrade path to a custom image build step rather than runtime configuration. Operators running the stock keycloak image (or any image built without the flag) get a hard failure of the update-compatibility tooling and, per the new CAUTION in advanced-configuration.adoc, the Operator itself; the failure surfaces only at upgrade time, not at deployment time, so an operator who enables spec.update.strategy=Recreate without rebuilding their image discovers the breakage during an actual upgrade attempt. While `Dockerfile-custom-image` also adds the flag to `kc.sh build`, the diff does not support the finding’s assertion that runtime flags/env/start args are absent or that only a custom image build step can enable the feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature-disabled path calls picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) and returns, but the exit code 4 is not in picocli.CommandLine.ExitCode's standard set and is undocumented as an error path distinct from the tool's compatibility verdicts, mixing 'configuration error' semantics into the same exit-code channel the tool uses for its documented result table. The update-compatibility guide's table now conflates compatibility outcomes (0-3) with a configuration prerequisite failure (4); consumers parsing the table cannot tell from the docs whether 4 is a verdict or an invocation error, and the ordering means a misconfigured invocation (feature off) is indistinguishable in kind from a compatibility finding, inviting scripts to treat FEATURE_DISABLED as a recreate verdict (the pre-existing meaning of 4).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a new exit code channel for a prerequisite failure: `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`/`UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` now do `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled, and `CompatibilityResult` defines `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` while also changing the compatibility verdict code `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3. Whether this is a defect is arguable (it’s a CLI contract/semantics and backward-compatibility concern rather than an immediate runtime correctness bug), but the finding’s core point—mixing an invocation/configuration error into the same numeric result space as compatibility outcomes and changing previously-used codes—is grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The docs template unconditionally appends --features=rolling-updates to every update-compatibility example, which becomes wrong the moment the feature is promoted to default/GA, and the template has no mechanism to reflect that state change. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature-disabled check calls picocli.exit(4) and returns before printPreviewWarning() and validateConfig() run, so a user invoking the command with both the feature disabled AND an invalid config gets only the feature message, masking the config error. Operators debugging why a compatibility check fails see only the 'rolling-updates is not enabled' error even when their configuration is also broken; after enabling the feature they hit the config error in a second, separate failure round-trip. This is minor but the ordering makes the first error report incomplete about the full set of problems.

adjudication.rationale: In both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(), the new guard `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { printFeatureDisabled(); picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED); return; }` is placed before `printPreviewWarning(); validateConfig();`. So the finding is accurate that config validation is skipped and only the feature-disabled message is shown when both conditions apply. This is an ordering/UX concern rather than a verifiable correctness defect, and it appears intentional (there is a new dist test `testFeatureNotEnabled` asserting this behavior).
